advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Count non-int-timestamp / non-dict-data skips in `_completion_phase_timestamps` under an audit key so absent phase timestamps are distinguishable from unparseable events.
evidence: Compare the sibling malformed path at line 475 which does `audit["bad_phase_event"] += 1`; the non-int-timestamp and non-dict-data skips have no counterpart audit signal, so an absent status_at is ambiguous between 'event not present' and 'event present but shape unexpected'.
advisory.finding: `_completion_phase_timestamps` silently skips any phase-event file whose top-level `timestamp` is not an int (`if not isinstance(timestamp_ns, int): continue`) without incrementing an audit counter, so a schema change to string/float timestamps would make status_at/signature_at vanish indistinguishably from 'no such event existed'.
scenarios: Tracker sidecar schema evolves timestamp to a float or ISO string; the probe reports empty verdict_to_status/status_to_signature phases with no diagnostic.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a classify_command test for the `sh -c`/`bash -lc` wrapper-unwrap branch (support lines 155-159).
evidence: Support code lines 155-159: `if Path(token).name in SHELLS: ... if tokens[flag_index] in {"-c", "-lc"} and flag_index + 1 < len(tokens): return classify_command(tokens[flag_index + 1], depth + 1)`
test_classify_command_separates_gate_operations_and_exclusions only exercises `rtk proxy rebar ...` and `rtk rebar ...` prefixes, never a `sh -c '...'` wrapper
Named violating input: `classify_command("sh -c 'rtk rebar review-plan sample-ticket'")` (or `bash -lc`)
advisory.finding: classify_command's shell-wrapper unwrap branch (recursing into a `sh -c`/`-lc` argument, support lines 155-159) is newly added but has no test; a command like `sh -c 'rtk rebar review-plan sample-ticket'` would exercise it and any regression in the nested-unwrap logic (e.g. off-by-one in the flag window or lost depth guard) would go undetected.
scenarios: A rollout where the model wraps the gate command in `bash -lc '...'`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a resolve_target test covering output-scraped ticket_id/`transitioned X:` extraction and the canonical-UUID fallback.
evidence: search for `resolve_target` in the test file returns `(no matches)`
test_attach_events_enforces_window_and_prefers_nearest_end pre-populates the alias map via `{"sample-ticket": "canonical"}` and never drives resolution from invocation.output

Named violating input: an Invocation whose `target` is None but whose output contains `transitioned 1111-2222-3333-4444:` — resolve_target must return the canonical id via the regex/UUID-fullmatch path
advisory.finding: resolve_target (support lines 580-592) is entirely untested: its output-derived candidate extraction (the `"ticket_id": "..."` regex, the `transitioned X:` regex) and the canonical-UUID fullmatch fallback have no coverage, so attach_events matching by output rather than by --target arg is unverified for newly-added code.
scenarios: A close invocation where the target is only discoverable from command output, not the parsed arg

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting main()/parser rejects `--since` later than `--until`.
evidence: rebar_duration_probe.py main(): `if args.since is not None and args.until is not None and args.since > args.until: parser.error("--since must not be later than --until")`
test_default_paths_are_repository_neutral only calls `probe._parser().parse_args([])` with no arguments and asserts defaults; no test exercises the since>until guard
advisory.finding: The CLI argument validation `--since must not be later than --until` in main() is newly added and untested; there is no test invoking the parser/main with an inverted window to assert the error is raised.
scenarios: Operator passes an inverted time window

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `ts_seconds` reject or explicitly UTC-normalize timezone-naive ISO strings rather than falling back to local-time interpretation.
evidence: A rollout/tracker timestamp emitted without an offset (e.g. '2026-08-23T17:27:03') becomes a naive datetime; `.timestamp()` then assumes local time, so on a non-UTC host all start/end/window values shift by the UTC offset.
blocking.finding: `ts_seconds` only normalizes a trailing 'Z' to '+00:00'; an ISO timestamp with no timezone designator is parsed as a naive datetime and `.timestamp()` interprets it in the host's LOCAL timezone, silently offsetting every derived duration/interval by the local UTC offset.
scenarios: Probe run on a developer machine set to a non-UTC timezone against logs that emit offset-less timestamps.
blocking.suggested_fix: After `fromisoformat`, if `dt.tzinfo is None` attach `timezone.utc` (or raise) before calling `.timestamp()`.
